subject: Follow-up: blobstore read audit confirmation
messages:
From: Amelia Barnett <amelia.barnett@kestrelbank.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Gavin Lowe <gavin.lowe@kestrelbank.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: File-store read audit request following outage

Logan —

Thanks for the quick response during the incident this morning. Kestrel needs a short written confirmation for our risk team: did any customer files (S3 objects / blobstore objects) get read, downloaded, or served externally as a result of the outage/mitigation actions? If you can’t confirm immediately, please provide an ETA and any interim mitigations you’ve applied.

We know you’ve done a cache purge; the compliance team is asking specifically about object-store GETs and any internal service principals that might have performed unexpected reads.

Appreciate a crisp, timebound reply — our deadline for the internal compliance note is EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Amelia Barnett
Head of Security Operations
Kestrel Bank

Attachments: none
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Barnett <amelia.barnett@kestrelbank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 13:40:22 -0700
Subject: Re: File-store read audit request following outage

Amelia —

Short update while our forensic sweep continues.

Summary (initial):
- We performed an emergency cache invalidation and a controlled restart of the file-proxy layer at 09:03 PDT. That action did not change object-store ACLs or issue new signed URLs.
- Preliminary access-log scan (service auth logs + S3 access logs) shows no anomalous GETs from external IPs during the incident window. All listed GET events were attributable to normal service worker activity and the cache rehydration process.
- We’ve exported a focused slice of object access logs for the window 08:45–10:15 and attached it: audit_log_export_20270801.csv.

What we’re doing next:
- Full hash reconciliation across object keys referenced in the incident (expected completion: tomorrow 15:00 PDT).
- Verification that no service principal used new/unauthorized credentials. Vivek is validating key rotation and token issuance logs.

We expect to provide a final attestation with the hash report and timeline by tomorrow afternoon.

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Barnett <amelia.barnett@kestrelbank.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: File-store read audit request following outage — final attestation

Amelia / Gavin —

This is the final attestation from Redwood’s incident and forensic team following the outage on 2027-08-01. We completed the tasks described below and have attached the supporting artifacts.

Findings (concise):
- Hash reconciliation: We computed SHA256 hashes for the set of object keys potentially referenced during the incident window and compared them against the last-known-good snapshot (taken 2027-07-30). No discrepancies were found. Detailed results are in hash_report_20270802.txt.
- Object access logs: The focused export (audit_log_export_20270801.csv) contains only expected GETs from our service worker pool and internal maintenance jobs. There were zero GET events from external/unknown IPs or principals for customer object keys.
- Credential issuance and scope: Token issuance logs show no ad-hoc token requests or elevated-scope grants during the incident. All tokens used during the window map to known service identities. Vivek validated key metadata and confirmed no key was leaked or rotated in a way that would indicate compromise.
- Artifact preservation: We captured the relevant VM snapshots, controller logs, and object-store access logs. Those artifacts are available in the Drive folder linked below for Kestrel’s auditors.

Conclusion (clear attestation):
Based on our log review, hash reconciliation, and credential audit, Redwood Inference confirms that no customer files were read, downloaded, or exfiltrated as a result of the incident or our mitigation actions. There is no evidence of unauthorized access to Kestrel Bank object-store data.

Attachments:
- audit_log_export_20270801.csv (CSV): focused object access events for 08:45–10:15 PDT.
- hash_report_20270802.txt (TXT): per-key hash reconciliation output.
- timeline_reconstruction_20270802.pdf (PDF): reconstructed timeline for the incident and actions taken.

Recommended follow-ups (optional):
- We suggest a short joint postmortem call to walk through findings and confirm any additional questions the Kestrel audit team may have. I’m available tomorrow morning 09:00–11:00 PDT or Wednesday afternoon.

If you’d like a signed attestation on Redwood letterhead, we can produce that for your compliance file — let us know.

Thanks,

Rachel Kim
Senior Security Engineer, Incident Response
Redwood Inference

--
Logan Wright
Incident Response Lead
Redwood Inference
